📊 Systemic Risk Regime Matrix — Maximum 44 Points
SCORE BAND REGIME LABEL TARGET PORTFOLIO ACTION MARKET ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERISTICS
0–3 Normal Risk Fully Invested / Risk-On Volatility is suppressed, credit spreads are tight, and market breadth is healthy. Asset allocation should favor maximum growth equity and high-beta exposure.
4–7 Correction Risk Tactical Neutral / Watch Early macro or technical cracks appearing (e.g., energy spikes or minor technical breakdown). Portfolio should pause new capital deployments and evaluate hedge triggers.
8–11 Systemic Stress Defensive Pivot / Hedges On Broader technical breakdown. Multiple asset classes are flashing warning signs (e.g., yields spiking or currency unwinding). Start moving capital into cash alternatives or defensive moats like AVGO and PLTR.
12–15 High Stress De-risking / Stress Plan Volatility enters a persistent high regime. High-yield credit markets begin to tighten significantly. Implement strict portfolio de-risking by trimming high-beta and leveraged assets.
16–25 High Risk De-risking / Stress Plan Broad-based market panic. Market breadth collapses completely, and correlation approaches 1. Portfolio focuses heavily on capital preservation and downside protection.
26–44 Systemic Risk Liquidity / Capitulation Full-scale institutional credit freeze, currency dislocation, or market crash. Liquidate remaining vulnerable exposures and prepare to deploy capital into deeply discounted structural moats as capitulation peaks.

Scoring v6.1 · Category limits remain 10 + 11 + 8 + 9 + 6 = 44. Narrow volatility curves, joint oil/yield pressure and conditional breadth deterioration are scored together. MOVE appears only in Volatility. These thresholds are heuristic, not optimized or validated crash probabilities. Historical graphs are recalculated using this same version.

⚡ Quick Paste Update- copy and paste this to your AI
Generate exactly 26 comma-separated values only (numbers; null for unavailable margin or volume fields) in the following order. Use the latest completed trading session and the latest published FINRA debt month. Use reported ^GSPC volume consistently; average the preceding 20 sessions excluding the current session. Debt changes compare the same series with 12 and 3 months earlier. Do not invent unavailable values:

VIX, VIX 1D %, VIX 5D %, HY OAS, HY OAS 5D bp change, HY OAS 20D bp change, BBB OAS, 10Y Yield, 10Y 20D bp change, S&P vs 50DMA, S&P vs 200DMA, WTI, WTI 20D %, MOVE, USDJPY, Breadth % >50DMA, Breadth 20D change, VIX 3M-1M spread, S&P 500 close, Margin debt reference month (YYYYMM), FINRA margin debt (USD million), Margin debt YoY %, Margin debt 3M change %, S&P reported volume, Prior 20-session volume average, S&P 500 daily change %
Generate Quick Paste from structured provider data

This converts normalized provider JSON; it does not connect to a live provider. Obtain the datasets from your chosen provider and map them to this template. Keys, units, dates and all 20 prior-session volumes are checked. Missing core indicators stop generation. Provider session completeness and data accuracy still require verification.

A specified date is saved at local noon to identify that observation day; this is not a market-data timestamp.

🔧 Manual Structural Overrides

Indicator explanations

D means trading days; DMA means daily moving average; bp means basis points (100 bp = 1 percentage point); pp means percentage points.

IndicatorUnitExplanation
VIXIndexExpected annualized S&P 500 volatility over the next 30 days, derived from options prices. Higher readings indicate greater expected movement, not its direction.
VIX 1D %%Percentage change in VIX from the previous trading day: (current / previous − 1) × 100. This is not the separate VIX1D index.
VIX 5D %%Percentage change in VIX over five trading days. A positive value means expected volatility has risen.
USDJPY carry-trade stressJPY per USD · 0–2 pointsA falling USDJPY means a stronger yen, which can pressure positions funded by borrowing yen. This model scores USDJPY ≤130: 2 points (red); >130 to 135: 1 (amber); >135: 0 (white). These fixed exchange-rate levels are a proxy, not direct evidence of carry-trade liquidation.
Margin leverage0–2 pointsUses FINRA customer margin debt. Buildup: year-over-year growth ≥20% earns 1 point; ≥40% earns 2. Deleveraging: three-month change ≤−5% earns 1; ≤−10% earns 2. Take the higher score, not their sum. Monthly debt does not measure total financial-system leverage. The reference month and debt amount inherit this component’s color; the date or dollar amount alone has no risk threshold.
Selling volume0–2 pointsDivide reported S&P volume by the average of the preceding 20 trading sessions, excluding the current day. If the S&P closes below its previous session: ratio ≥1.5 earns 1 point; ≥2 earns 2. Otherwise 0. Volume, average volume and daily return inherit this component’s color. Heavy volume alone does not confirm forced selling or a market bottom.
USDJPY momentum diagnostic% over 3 FX sessions(USDJPY / value 3 available FX observations earlier − 1) × 100. Negative means yen appreciation. Amber at −1.5%, red at −3%. Diagnostic only; not extra score points.
200DMA distance velocity5-session change in ppToday’s S&P percentage distance from its own 200DMA minus the distance 5 equity sessions earlier. Each moving average uses only information then available. Below the 200DMA, a loss of 3 pp flags watch and 5 pp flags stress. Not proof of forced liquidation and not extra points.
Margin debt / reference monthUSD million / YYYYMMAggregate customer securities-margin debit balances from FINRA. Monthly, not daily; use a published report or the explicitly assumed two-month lag for historical data.
Margin debt YoY / 3M change%(Current debt / debt 12 or 3 months earlier − 1) × 100. Leverage points: maximum of YoY ≥20% → 1, ≥40% → 2; 3M ≤−5% → 1, ≤−10% → 2. Maximum 2, not the sum.
Reported volume / prior 20D averageSharesYahoo ^GSPC reported-volume proxy. Average the preceding 20 trading sessions, excluding the signal day. Keep the same provider and units.
Volume ratio / selling pressureRatio / 0–2 pointsVolume divided by prior 20D average. On a negative S&P daily return: ratio ≥1.5 adds 1 point; ≥2 adds 2. Otherwise 0. Missing inputs produce a score range.
S&P 500 daily change%(Current closing level / previous trading-session close − 1) × 100. Used to distinguish selling volume from rising-price volume.
Possible volume exhaustionObservationAt least 2× volume, a new 20-session low, close above the open and in the top 30% of the day’s range. A possible reversal, not a confirmed bottom; adds no separate points.
HY OASbpHigh-yield corporate bond option-adjusted spread over a Treasury benchmark, adjusted for embedded options. Wider spreads indicate greater credit stress.
HY OAS 5D bp changebpCurrent high-yield OAS minus its value five trading days ago. Positive values mean spreads widened.
HY OAS 20D bp changebpCurrent high-yield OAS minus its value twenty trading days ago. Positive values mean spreads widened.
BBB OASbpOption-adjusted spread for BBB-rated investment-grade corporate bonds. Higher readings indicate more credit risk priced into these bonds.
10Y Yield%Yield on the 10-year US Treasury. Enter 4.80 for 4.80%. This dashboard assigns more risk points to higher yields.
10Y 20D bp changebpChange in 10-year Treasury yield over twenty trading days. A move from 4.50% to 4.80% is 30 basis points.
S&P vs 50DMA%S&P 500 distance from its 50-day moving average: (index / average − 1) × 100. Negative values mean the index is below its average.
S&P vs 200DMA%S&P 500 distance from its 200-day moving average, using the same formula. Negative values indicate weakness versus the longer-term trend.
WTIUSD/barrelWest Texas Intermediate crude oil price. Use the same spot or futures series for all entries and its 20-day change. This dashboard flags high oil prices as a macro stress signal.
WTI 20D %%Oil momentum: 20-session rise ≥10% earns 1 point; ≥20% earns 2. Add 1 when WTI ≥$90 and 10Y yield ≥4.50%, capped at 2 points for this component. A joint level trigger signals overlapping pressure; it is not a measured correlation. The WTI and yield level components are retained.
MOVEIndexICE BofA bond-market implied-volatility index based on US Treasury options. Higher values indicate greater expected interest-rate volatility.
USDJPYJPY/USDJapanese yen per US dollar. A lower value means a stronger yen; this dashboard uses low levels as a carry-trade stress signal.
Breadth % >50DMA%Percentage of S&P 500 constituents above their own 50-day moving averages. Lower values indicate fewer stocks participating in the uptrend.
Breadth 20D changeppCurrent breadth minus its value 20 trading sessions earlier, in percentage points. Loss ≤−10 pp: 2 points. Otherwise, loss ≤−4 pp with current breadth <65%: 1 point; otherwise 0. This flags deteriorating participation even before an index breaks its trend.
VIX 3M-1M spreadIndex pointsVIX3M minus 30-day VIX, in index points; these are implied-volatility indices, not front-month futures. Negative spread: 2 points. A nonnegative spread <1.0 with VIX 5D change >10% also earns 2. Otherwise spread <1.5 earns 1; ≥1.5 earns 0. Zero is flat, not backwardation. This measures a narrow curve, not its rate of flattening; both inputs should be from the same closing session.

S&P 500 close: the closing level of the S&P 500 price index; shown for comparison and excluded from the risk score. Context: Cboe implied-volatility term structure · Federal Reserve: borrowing costs and economic activity. Reference definitions: Cboe volatility indices · ICE MOVE · ICE bond methodology. Risk colors follow this dashboard’s existing scoring rules.

Current and past entries

Saved when you select Parse & Update or Save Manual Changes. Newest entry first. Use the red × to delete a row after confirmation. Deleting the current saved entry restores the latest remaining entry, or sample defaults if none remain. Edit a saved row’s date, time or indicator values, then select Save. Its composite score is calculated from 18 market indicators plus margin leverage and volume selling pressure (44 points maximum). Rows are reordered by date; the newest saved row supplies the current dashboard values. Unavailable added inputs display as a score range, never as assumed zero. Dates default to entry time and can be changed to your observation time, in , not when the market data was published. Units appear in column headings; value cells contain numbers only.

White: no risk points · Amber: intermediate risk points · Red: maximum risk points. Composite score colors: white 0–3, amber 4–11, red 12–44. Hover over a value for its score.

S&P 500 closes are matched to the displayed entry date, using the previous session for weekends, holidays, or a session not yet closed. Hover over a price for its actual session date. Green lines on all graphs show daily closes on an independent right-hand price axis. Price data is embedded through September 23, 2026; later unavailable dates are blank unless entered by you; this embedded dataset does not refresh automatically. Source: Yahoo Finance S&P 500. Quick Paste accepts 26 values, including the margin-debt and volume fields listed above. You can also enter or edit the price manually; it is saved and synced with the entry. The latest saved price for a date overrides its sourced price on your six current-history graphs. Prices do not affect risk scores.

History syncs to your account automatically every 8 minutes while logged in (and via "Sync now"), so it follows you across devices. It's still cached locally too, so it survives a refresh even offline. Default sample values are not saved automatically.

Composite crash risk over time

Shows saved entries within the selected period ending now, using their edited dates and local time. Unsaved changes and future-dated entries are excluded. Hover or focus on a point for its date and score.
